english.title: Assistant to blind voter communicate information relating to vote
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having undertaken to assist a blind voter to vote, communicated to a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), information as to the

(A)_[candidate for whom that voter intended to vote]_
(B)_[candidate for whom that voter had voted]_
(C)_[registered political party towards the return of whose candidates that voter intended to vote]_
(D)_[registered political party towards the return of whose candidates that voter had voted]_
(E)_[number on the back of the ballot paper given for the use of that voter]_
(F)_[unique identifying mark on the back of the ballot paper given for the use of that voter]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 66(5) and (6) of the Representation of the People Act 1983.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
having undertaken to assist a blind voter to vote
communicated to a person information as to the candidate for whom or registered political party towards the return of whose candidates
that voter intended to vote or had voted, or
as to the number or other unique identifying mark on the back of the ballot paper given for the use of that voter

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Options C and D relate to an election of the London members of the London Assembly, as per subsection 66(7) of the Act.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine.Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex see section 176Note
On the 12th March 2015, the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' Court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
